'''DeMarcus Amir Cousins''' (born August 13, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the Selenge Bodons of the [[The League (Mongolia)|Mongolian Basketball League]]. Nicknamed "'''Boogie'''",<ref>{{cite news |title=SportsThat: DeMarcus Cousins on ESPN's First Take|publisher=sportsthat.blogspot.com|date=July 27, 2010|access-date=July 3, 2018|url=http://sportsthat.blogspot.com/2010/07/dearcus-cousins-on-espns-frist-take.html|quote=Coach Rod Strickland at Kentucky gave me the name. I would be playing ball and I would do moves that guards would do and coach Strickland said, "Man, you got a lot of Boogie." Every time I walked into the gym he would say, "What's up Boogie!" and it just stuck.}}</ref> he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]], earning consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors in 2010. He left Kentucky after his freshman season, and was selected with the fifth overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. In his first season with the Kings, Cousins was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]], and from 2015 to 2018, he was named an [[NBA All-Star]] four times. He is also a two-time gold medal winner as a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]], winning his first in 2014 at the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]] and his second in 2016 at the [[2016 Summer Olympics|Rio Olympics]].

==High school career==
Cousins attended [[LeFlore Magnet High School]] in [[Mobile, Alabama]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/couside01.html|title= DeMarcus Cousins NBA Stats|work= Basketball-Reference.com |access-date= November 10, 2012}}</ref> He was a first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] in 2009 and played in the [[2009 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], finishing with 14 points and 8 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/highschoolsports/2008969865_webhoopagatewed02.html?syndication=rss |title=Wednesday's McDonald's All-American Game box scores |publisher=Seattletimes.nwsource.com |date=April 2, 2009 |access-date=March 22, 2010}}</ref> Cousins also played in the 2009 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] at the [[Rose Garden (arena)|Rose Garden]] in [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]] and the Jordan Brand Classic at [[Madison Square Garden]] where he scored 10 points for the black team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4080678|title=Big men shine in Jordan Brand Classic |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=April 19, 2009 |access-date=December 4, 2012}}</ref> He led LeFlore to the Alabama class 6A Final Four, falling short in the semifinal game to future college teammate [[Eric Bledsoe]] and [[Parker High School (Alabama)|Parker High School]].

==College career==
[[File:DeMarcus Cousins.jpg|thumb|150px|right|Cousins with [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] in 2009]]
Cousins first committed to [[UAB Blazers men's basketball|Alabama-Birmingham]] on February 28, 2008, but never signed a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.al.com/spotnews/2008/02/top_prospect_cousins_commits_t.html |title=Top basketball prospect DeMarcus Cousins commits to UAB |publisher=Blog.al.com |date=February 29, 2008 |access-date=March 22, 2010}}</ref> Cousins decommitted from UAB and committed to [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] on March 9, 2009.<ref>{{cite magazine |author=Seth Davis, SI.com |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/basketball/ncaa/03/08/cousins.memphis/index.html |title=Prep standout Cousins commits to Memphis |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=March 8, 2009 |access-date=March 22, 2010 |archive-date=March 14, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100314133343/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/basketball/ncaa/03/08/cousins.memphis/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He reopened his recruitment after then Memphis coach [[John Calipari]] was hired at Kentucky. On April 7, 2009, Cousins decided to follow John Calipari to Kentucky.<ref>{{cite web|last=Calle |first=Franklyn |url=http://slamonline.com/online/college-hs/college/2009/04/demarcus-cousins-to-kentucky/ |title=DeMarcus Cousins To Kentucky |publisher=Slamonline.com |date=April 9, 2009 |access-date=March 22, 2010}}</ref> He signed his letter of intent on April 15. At Kentucky, Cousins averaged 15.1 points, 9.8 rebounds and 1.8 blocks per game. Led by Cousins and [[John Wall]], the Wildcats reached the [[Elite Eight]] of the [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2010 NCAA Tournament]].

==Professional career==
===Sacramento Kings (2010–2017)===
====2010–14: All-Rookie honors and controversies====
On April 7, 2010, Cousins announced that he would forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2010 NBA draft]], where he was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the fifth overall pick.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/couside01.html|title= DeMarcus Amir Cousins|publisher= Basketball-Reference.Com |access-date= November 10, 2012}}</ref> On July 7, 2010, Cousins signed his rookie contract with the Kings, worth about $7 million for the first two years with a team option for the third and fourth years.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5362116|title=Kings sign top draft pick Cousins |publisher=ESPN|date=July 7, 2010 |access-date=February 27, 2020}}</ref> Cousins was named the Rookie of the Month for July during the [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/07/18/cousins.rom/index.html?rss=true |title=Kings' Cousins named Rookie of Month for July |publisher=NBA |date=July 18, 2010 |access-date=November 12, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110215007/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/07/18/cousins.rom/index.html?rss=true |archive-date=November 10, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Cousins was also named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] at the end of the 2010–11 season.

On January 1, 2012, head coach [[Paul Westphal]] sent Cousins home from the Kings' home game against the [[New Orleans Hornets]], saying that Cousins was "unwilling/unable to embrace traveling in the same direction as his team; it cannot be ignored indefinitely."<ref>{{cite news|number=153618274331004928|title= Westphal: "...unwilling/unable to embrace traveling in the same direction as his team, it cannot be ignored indefinitely."|first=Sam|last=Amick|date=January 1, 2012 }}</ref> Cousins, who had been averaging 13.0 points and 11.3 rebounds per game at the time of the dismissal, reportedly demanded to be traded from the Kings. Cousins later denied asking to be traded.

On January 5, 2012, Westphal was fired from the Kings, leading many to speculate that the head coach's tumultuous relationship with Cousins was a factor in his being replaced.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7428725/sacramento-kings-fire-paul-westphal-sign-keith-smart|title=Paul Westphal fired after 2–5 start |publisher=ESPN|date=January 6, 2012 |access-date=February 27, 2020}}</ref> On February 8, 2012, Cousins was selected to play in the [[NBA All-Star Weekend Rookie Challenge|Rising Stars Challenge]]. He played for Team [[Charles Barkley|Chuck]], with a mix of rookies and sophomores.[[File:DeMarcus Cousins Andrew Bogut.jpg|thumb|left|Cousins with [[Andrew Bogut]]]]
On November 11, 2012, the league suspended Cousins for two games without pay for confronting [[San Antonio Spurs]] color commentator [[Sean Elliott]] "in a hostile manner" after he criticized Cousins for attempting to bully [[Tim Duncan]] on the court.<ref>{{cite web|last=Helin |first=Kurt |url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/11/12/players-union-appeals-demarcus-cousins-suspension/ |title=Players union appeals DeMarcus Cousins suspension |website=ProBasketballTalk|date=November 12, 2012 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> Cousins was apparently informed of Elliott's remarks after the game. He left the locker room and waited on the court for Elliott to finish his post-game show before confronting him. Some criticized the suspension as overly harsh and based more on Cousins' reputation than what actually happened, while others said he needed to grow up and learn a lesson about confronting the media.<ref>{{cite web|author=Eric Freeman |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/demarcus-cousins-got-confusing-suspension-confronting-spurs-commentator-033627383--nba.html |title=DeMarcus Cousins got a confusing suspension for confronting Spurs commentator Sean Elliott |website=Sports.yahoo.com |date=November 12, 2012 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> Cousins apologized to Elliott in person before a game against the Spurs in March 2014, which Elliott said he appreciated.<ref>{{cite web|last=Helin |first=Kurt |url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/03/22/demarcus-cousins-delivers-unexpected-apology-to-spurs-broadcaster-sean-elliott-for-last-seasons-incident/ |title=DeMarcus Cousins delivers unexpected apology to Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott for last season's incident |website=ProBasketballTalk |date=March 22, 2014 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref>

On December 22, 2012, Cousins was suspended indefinitely from the Kings, who accused him of "unprofessional behavior and conduct detrimental to the team".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8772913/sacramento-kings-suspend-demarcus-cousins-indefinitely-conduct|title=Sacramento Kings suspend DeMarcus Cousins indefinitely for conduct |website=ESPN |date=December 23, 2012 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> The suspension was lifted on December 24, 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8778226/demarcus-cousins-reinstated-sacramento-kings|title=DeMarcus Cousins reinstated by Sacramento Kings |website=ESPN|date=December 24, 2012 |access-date=February 27, 2020}}</ref> The season was up-and-down for Cousins, who posted career-highs in [[Player Efficiency Rating]], field goal percentage, and free throw percentage, but led the NBA with 16 [[technical foul]]s, was ejected several times and suspended by both the league and the Kings.[[File:DeMarcus Cousins Dec 2013.jpg|thumb|Cousins with the Kings in December 2013]]
On September 30, 2013, Cousins signed a reported four-year, $62 million contract extension with the Kings.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9750405/demarcus-cousins-signs-4-year-contract-extension-sacramento-kings|title=DeMarcus Cousins signs 4-year contract extension with Sacramento Kings |website=ESPN|date=September 30, 2013 |access-date=February 27, 2020}}</ref> After signing the contract, Cousins announced he would donate $1 million of his salary to the families and community of Sacramento.<ref>{{cite web |author=CRAIG MASSEI |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/kings-sign-demarcus-cousins-4-184524223--nba.html |title=Kings sign DeMarcus Cousins to 4-year extension |website=Sports.yahoo.com |date=September 30, 2013 |access-date=August 21, 2016 |archive-date=March 5, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305114456/https://sports.yahoo.com/news/kings-sign-demarcus-cousins-4-184524223--nba.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He opened the season with a 30-point, 14-rebound performance against the [[Denver Nuggets]].

On February 26, 2014, Cousins received a one-game suspension for punching [[Patrick Beverley]] in the stomach. On March 11, Cousins recorded a career-high 6 blocks, along with 13 points and 14 rebounds, in an 89–99 loss to the Detroit Pistons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20140311/SACDET/gameinfo.html |title=Kings at Pistons – March 11, 2014 – Game Preview, Play by Play, Scores and Recap on |website=Nba.com |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref>

====2014–16: First All-Star and All-NBA appearances====
After averaging career-highs of 23.5 points, 12.6 rebounds and 1.5 blocks over the first 15 games of the season, Cousins was diagnosed with viral meningitis on December 7, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11994229/demarcus-cousins-sacramento-kings-missed-five-games-viral-meningitis|title= DeMarcus Cousins recovering slowly|website=ESPN|date=December 7, 2014 |access-date=February 27, 2020}}</ref> He subsequently missed 10 games with the virus and showed no signs of a let up in his return to action on December 18 against the Milwaukee Bucks as he recorded 27 points and 11 rebounds in the 107–108 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20141218/MILSAC/gameinfo.html |title=Bucks at Kings – December 18, 2014|website=NBA.com|date= December 18, 2014 |access-date=February 27, 2020}}</ref>

On January 30, 2015, Cousins was named to replace the injured [[Kobe Bryant]] as a Western Conference All-Star in the [[2015 NBA All-Star Game]]. Cousins' selection marked the first time a Kings player earned All-Star honors since [[Brad Miller (basketball)|Brad Miller]] and [[Peja Stojaković]] represented Sacramento in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/cousins-2015-allstar |title=DeMarcus Cousins Named to 2015 NBA All-Star Team|website=NBA|date=January 30, 2015 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref>

On April 1, 2015, Cousins recorded his second career triple-double with 24 points, 21 rebounds, 10 assists, 6 blocks and 3 steals in a 111–115 loss to the Houston Rockets.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150401/SACHOU/gameinfo.html |title=Kings at Rockets – April 1, 2015 – Game Preview, Play by Play, Scores and Recap on |website=Nba.com |access-date=August 21, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630070942/http://www.nba.com/games/20150401/SACHOU/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 30, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In doing so, he became just the fourth player in NBA history to collect 20+ points, 20+ rebounds, 10+ assists and 5+ blocks in a single game, joining [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]], [[Chris Webber]] and [[Tim Duncan]]. In the following game on April 3 against the New Orleans Pelicans, Cousins became the first Kings player to record back-to-back triple doubles since Chris Webber did so in 2005. In just under 42 minutes of action, he recorded 24 points, 20 rebounds and a career-high 13 assists in a 95–101 loss. He joined elite company as one of only three players to have consecutive 20-point, 20-rebound, 10-assist games; the others being [[Elgin Baylor]] and [[Wilt Chamberlain]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20150403/NOPSAC/gameinfo.html |title=Pelicans at Kings – April 3, 2015 – Game Preview, Play by Play, Scores and Recap on |website=Nba.com |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref>

On October 28, 2015, Cousins recorded 32 points and 13 rebounds, as well as 4-of-5 three-pointers, in a season opening loss to the Los Angeles Clippers. Cousins had hit just four three-pointers in his previous 167 games and had never hit more than four in an entire season.<ref>{{cite On January 4, 2016, Cousins recorded 33 points and a season-high 19 rebounds in a 116–104 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160104/SACOKC/gameinfo.html|title=Cousins has 33 points, 19 boards, Kings top Thunder 116–104|work=NBA.com|date=January 4, 2016|access-date=January 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160103204431/http://www.nba.com/games/20160104/SACOKC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 3, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 21, in a win over the Atlanta Hawks, he recorded 24 points and 15 rebounds for his ninth straight double-double and his 24th of the season in 34 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160121/ATLSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Cousins has 24 points, 15 rebounds as Kings beat Hawks 91–88|work=NBA.com|date=January 21, 2016|access-date=January 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125053241/http://www.nba.com/games/20160121/ATLSAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 25, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 23, he scored a career-high 48 points in a 108–97 win over the Indiana Pacers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160123/INDSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Cousins scores career high 48 as Kings beat Pacers 108–97|work=NBA.com|date=January 23, 2016|access-date=January 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160124101153/http://www.nba.com/games/20160123/INDSAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 24, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 25, he was named Western Conference Player of the Week for a second time in 2015–16.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/cousins-western-conference-player-week|title=Cousins Named Western Conference Player of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=January 25, 2016|access-date=November 28, 2016}}</ref> He went on to top his career-high mark in emphatic fashion that night, scoring 56 points in a 129–128 double overtime loss to the Charlotte Hornets. His 56 points set a record for the 2015–16 season, and broke [[Chris Webber]]'s franchise record of 51 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160125/CHASAC/gameinfo.html|title=Cousins scores 56, sets Sacramento record in double-OT loss|work=NBA.com|date=January 25, 2016|access-date=January 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126123342/http://www.nba.com/games/20160125/CHASAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 26, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 28, he was named a Western Conference All-Star reserve for the [[2016 NBA All-Star Game]], earning his second straight All-Star nod.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/demarcus-cousins-named-2016-all-star|title=DeMarcus Cousins Named To 2016 NBA Western Conference All-Star Team|work=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2016|access-date=January 29, 2016}}</ref> On February 5, he recorded his first triple-double of the season and fourth of his career with 24 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 128–119 loss to the Brooklyn Nets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/kings-lose-nets-three|title=Kings Unable To Cool Red-Hot Nets|work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2016|access-date=February 5, 2016}}</ref> On February 19, he had 37 points, 20 rebounds and four blocks against the Denver Nuggets, recording his ninth career double-double with 20-plus points and rebounds, breaking the previous Sacramento record set by Webber.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/DENSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Cousin has 37 points, 20 rebounds in Kings' win over Nuggets|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2016|access-date=February 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222213843/http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/DENSAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 22, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2016–17: Final season in Sacramento====
In the Kings' season opener on October 26, Cousins scored a game-high 24 points in a 113–94 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899412|title=Cousins, Gay lead Kings past young Suns 113–94|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 27, 2016}}</ref> He backed that up On January 13, 2023, the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] hosted Cousins for a workout.<ref>{{cite web |title=Reports: Centres Cousins and Leonard to workout for Lakers on Friday |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/reports-centres-cousins-and-leonard-to-workout-for-lakers-on-friday/ |website=SportsNet.ca |access-date=January 14, 2023 |date=January 12, 2023}}</ref>

===Mets de Guaynabo (2023)===
In April 2023, Cousins signed a contract to join the [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Guaynabo Mets]] in [[Puerto Rico]]'s [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] league.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DeMarcus Cousins joins Guaynabo Mets in Puerto Rican league |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2023/04/11/demarcus-cousins-joins-guaynabo-mets-in-puerto-rican-league/70104217007/ |date=April 11, 2023 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref> During the 2023 season he averaged 20.4 points, 10.9 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game in 25.48 minutes per game. He shot 44% from the 3 point line, and 69% in free throws.<ref>{{Cite web |title= BSN Estadisticas Jugadores Cousins, DeMarcus |url=https://www.bsnpr.com/jugadores/jugador?id=13485&e=14 |date=July 17, 2023 |website=Baloncesto Superior Nacional |language=es}}</ref> Cousins led the team to the Playoffs and semi-finals but was unable to make the finals after being eliminated by the [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] in 7 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title= Gigantes eliminan a los Mets y pasan a la final de BSN |url=https://www.primerahora.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/gigantes-eliminan-a-los-mets-y-pasan-a-la-final-de-bsn/ |date=July 16, 2023 |website=Primera Hora |language=es}}</ref> He was injured at the beginning of Game 6 with the expectation of being out for one week.<ref>{{Cite web |title= DeMarcus Cousins suffers injury in game 6 of semifinals in Puerto Rico |url=https://www.nationofblue.com/demarcus-cousins-suffers-injury-in-game-6-of-semifinals-in-puerto-rico/ |date=July 16, 2023 |website=Nation of Blue |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Taiwan Beer Leopards (2024)===
On December 18, 2023, Cousins signed a contract to join the [[Taiwan Beer Leopards]] in [[Taiwan]]'s [[T1 League]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Li |first1=Chien-chung |last2=Mazzetta |first2=Matthew |title=BASKETBALL/Taiwan Beer Leopards sign former NBA player DeMarcus Cousins |url=https://focustaiwan.tw/sports/202312180011 |access-date=December 19, 2023 |agency=Central News Agency |date=December 18, 2023}} Republished as: {{cite news |title=T1 League's Taiwan Beer Leopards sign former NBA player DeMarcus Cousins |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2023/12/19/2003810836 |access-date=December 19, 2023 |work=Taipei Times |date=December 19, 2023}}</ref> The plan was to initially compete in four home games scheduled for January 2024, with the decision to continue participating based on Cousins.

On February 23, 2024, Cousins announced that he is done trying to make an [[NBA]] comeback. When a reporter had asked him if he plans on returning to the NBA in an interview, Cousins said "Honestly, no. I know I’ve had my time there. You know, there was a point where I was trying to make that happen. But the place I'm in my life now, just with everything I’ve got going on, just outside of basketball, like I'm in a good place. So, like I said, I'm excited for what I have ahead and my future. You know, my 12 years in the league were a small chapter or chapters in my life. And, I'm ready to move on to the next and see what's in store for me."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kumar |first=Vishwesha |title=Demarcus Cousins Has Officially Announced His NBA Retirement |url=https://fadeawayworld.net/demarcus-cousins-done-nba-after-12-years |access-date=March 11, 2024 |work=Fadeaway World |date=February 24, 2024}}</ref> On March 18, Cousins re-signed with the [[Taiwan Beer Leopards]].<ref>{{cite news |title=表弟回來了！雲豹宣布續約 卡森斯預計4月中抵台 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2702177 |accessdate=March 18, 2024 |work=ETtoday |date=March 18, 2024}}</ref> On May 15, Cousins was awarded the [[T1 League]] Most Popular Player of the Year for the [[2023–24 T1 League season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=「表弟」卡森斯擠下阿巴西 摘下T1聯盟年度人氣王！ |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2739192 |accessdate=May 15, 2024 |work=ETtoday |date=May 15, 2024}}</ref> On June 1, Cousins was awarded the Finals MVP in the [[2024 T1 League Finals]].<ref>{{cite news |title=表弟卡森斯勇奪冠軍賽MVP 雲豹隊史首冠宣布發730萬獎金 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2750370 |accessdate=June 1, 2024 |work=ETtoday |date=June 1, 2024}}</ref>

On June 19, 2024, Cousins joined the Taiwan Mustangs of The Asian Tournament (TAT).<ref>{{cite news|title=找庫克、卡森斯助拳 「魔獸」領軍台灣野馬隊拚冠 |url=https://udn.com/news/story/7003/8040607 |accessdate=June 19, 2024 |work=United Daily News |date=June 19, 2024}}</ref>

===Selenge Bodons (2025)===
On January 10, 2025, Cousins signed with the Selenge Bodons of [[The League (Mongolia)|The League]] in Mongolia.<ref>{{cite web |title='NBA 폭군' 드마커스 커즌스, 전 삼성 강바일과 함께 뛴다···몽골리그 진출 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065594987332920 |website=점프볼 |access-date=January 10, 2025 |date=January 10, 2025}}</ref> Meanwhile, he briefly joined the [[Strong Group Athletics]] in the [[Dubai]] International Basketball Championship.

===Second stint with Guaynabo (2025)===
On April 24, 2025, it was confirmed that Cousins was returning to play for the [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Guaynabo Mets]] for the 2025 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Modestti |first1=Luis |title=Guaynabo changes their imports, Cousins comes back |url=https://basketball.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/news/930348/Guaynabo-changes-their-imports-Cousins-comes-back#google_vignette |website=latinbasket.com |access-date=April 24, 2025}}</ref>  On May 6, he played his first game back with the Mets against [[Capitanes de Arecibo]], where he recorded 11 points, 9 rebounds and 8 assists in just 21 minutes, helping Guaynabo win 107–90.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mets hunden a los Capitanes en el regreso de Demarcus Cousins |url=https://www.telemundopr.com/historias-destacadas/mets-hunden-a-los-capitanes-en-el-regreso-de-demarcus-cousins/2714482/ |website=telemundopr.com |access-date=May 6, 2025}}</ref> On 10 June, Cousins was restrained after clashing with fans who had thrown beer on him.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DeMarcus Cousins Restrained After Fan Clash in Puerto Ric... |url=https://www.complex.com/sports/a/markelibert/demarcus-cousins-restrained-after-fans-throw-beer-at-him-in-puerto-rico |access-date=2025-06-10 |website=Complex |language=en}}</ref> He was later suspended for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-10 |title=DeMarcus Cousins suspended for rest of season |url=https://hoopshype.com/2025/06/10/demarcus-cousins-suspended-for-rest-of-season/ |access-date=2025-06-10 |website=HoopsHype |language=en-US}}</ref> On June 11, the Mets terminated Cousins’ contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=DeMarcus Cousins suspended for season, contract terminated after brawl with fans|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/demarcus-cousins-suspended-season-contract-205045563.html|website=sports.yahoo.com|date=June 11, 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:DeMarcus Cousins with the Team USA in 2014.jpg|thumb|upright|right|Cousins with Team USA in 2014]]
Cousins was a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] that won the gold medal at the [[2014 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Moore |first=Matt |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24674782/team-usa-announces-2014-final-roster-lillard-parsons-cut |title=Team USA announces 2014 final roster: Lillard, Parsons cut |website=CBSSports.com |date=August 23, 2014 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> He won a second gold medal with the [[2016 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2016 Olympic team]] in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.<ref>{{cite web|last=Amick|first=Sam|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/rio-2016/2016/08/21/usa-defeats-serbia-gold-medal-game-kevin-durant/89079370/|title=Kevin Durant, USA blow out Serbia to win Olympic gold|work=USA Today|date=August 21, 2016|access-date=October 12, 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Cousins is the son of Monique and Jessie Cousins.<ref name="usab">{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/c/cousins-demarcus.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618223733/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/c/cousins-demarcus.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 18, 2015|title=DeMarcus Cousins|work=usab.com|access-date=January 4, 2017}}</ref> He has four sisters and one brother, [[Jaleel Cousins|Jaleel]], who is also a professional basketball player.<ref name="usab" /><ref>{{cite web|last1=Jones|first1=Jason|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/kings-blog/article84647132.html|title=Jaleel Cousins hopes to distinguish himself from brother DeMarcus|work=Sacbee.com|access-date=October 17, 2016|date=June 18, 2016}}</ref>

Cousins has two children. He married his longtime girlfriend Morgan Lang in Atlanta on August 24, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.com/sports/demarcus-cousins-marries-morgan-lang/|title=DeMarcus Cousins Is Married! Lakers Star Weds Longtime Love Morgan Lang in Atlanta Wedding|website=PEOPLE.com|access-date=August 27, 2019}}</ref>

In August 2019, Cousins was captured on an audio recording threatening to kill his ex-girlfriend after she refused to let their son attend his wedding.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2019/08/27/demarcus-cousins-death-threat-ex-girlfriend/2130774001/|title=DeMarcus Cousins' alleged death threat to ex-girlfriend under investigation|website=[[USA Today]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.tmz.com/2019/08/27/demarcus-cousins-accused-threatening-shoot-baby-mama-before-wedding/| title = DeMarcus Cousins Audio Allegedly Threatening to Shoot Baby Mama Before Wedding}}</ref> An arrest warrant was placed on Cousins for a [[misdemeanor]] [[Domestic violence in the United States|domestic violence]] charge and a third-degree harassing communications charge.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/lakers/2019/08/29/demarcus-cousins-arrest-warrant-issued-domestic-violence-charge/2153548001/|title=DeMarcus Cousins sought on arrest warrant for domestic violence charge|website=amp.usatoday.com|access-date=August 30, 2019}}</ref> The charges, filed in Alabama, were dropped in November.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ganguli |first1=Tania |title=Lakers center DeMarcus Cousins will not face harassment charges, attorney says |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2019-11-22/lakers-center-demarcus-cousins-will-not-face-charges |website=Los Angeles Times |access-date=February 24, 2020 |date=November 22, 2019}}</ref>
